page: Amazon Web Services m8i-flex.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 64 vCPUs and 32 physical cores, utilizing the Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong capabilities across compute and memory-intensive tasks. The instance achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core performance and image processing, alongside strong multi-core performance in stress-ng and Passmark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth benchmarks show strong read performance for both small and large blocks, though large block write performance remains in the average tier. The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and matrix operations, which is reflected in strong LLM inference speeds for small and medium models, and top-tier prompt processing for large 70B models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8i-flex family provides a balanced resource density of 4 GB RAM per vCPU, making it a viable option for workloads requiring modern DDR5 memory and high-frequency Intel Xeon processors without the premium of dedicated local storage or GPU accelerators. Appropriate workloads include static web serving, software compilation, database operations, and moderate-scale language model inference.
